I'm an older adult who experienced a very sudden vision symptom -- one which could rapidly lead to sudden blindness.  I went to St Peter Eye Hospital for diagnosis and possible treatment.  My experience there was excellent, and I highly recommend them.

HERE'S MY STORY:

My scary symptom was sudden-onset floaters in my left eye combined with light flashes in the same eye.  I discovered these symptoms could be indications of a detached retina.  My USA ophthalmologist directed me to have this checked out immediately -- it might be something minor or it be something that might rip further at any time causing blindness in one eye.  This definitely got my attention and created some natural anxiety.

I reached out to several friends I trust here in Chiang Mai for recommendations and insights. They each recommended Dr. Kupakanjana at St Peter Eye Hospital based either on personal first-hand experience or word of mouth.

Although he had just landed that day from a flight, Dr. Kupakanjana (or Dr. Nickie for short), took my call that afternoon.  He then had his staff make an appointment for me the next morning.  I received a thorough examination (actually several types of exams).  The news I received was mixed -- no emergency or risk of sudden blindness, but instead an age-related degeneration that might continue to advance over time (much like a mole on my retina).  But I was very relieved.  I also appreciated the professionalism of the staff there and the time Dr. Nickie took to explain the problem and my future options.  By noon I was finished and able to return to my apartment with my wife (my eye was dilated from one of the exams).

The cost for his services was very fair.  As an indication of the value at St Peter --  I ordered two pair of bifocal prescription sunglasses while I was there because they were a better value than the optical stores I had visited in town.  This was unrelated to my emergency visit, but I felt good enough about my care that I made these additional optional purchases.

Note: there were a few reviews I read (only a handful of 1-star reviews) about St Peter that gave me pause as I did my initial research about selecting an eye doctor.  I realized those reviews were ALL old 5+ years and with a different doctor.  Recommend you google Dr. Kupakanjana and note his credentials and record.  He came from a strong practice elsewhere to Chiang Mai for family reasons.  I feel very fortunate that he relocated here!
I went for a color blindness test that took less than 20 minutes and cost 650 baht, and I didn't get any advice other than the doctor saying I'm truly color blind.

For about three years, I'd been feeling frustrated and annoyed with the difficulties of daily routines and driving because I had to switch glasses for reading and driving, both day and night. So, I consulted an ophthalmologist about how to make life easier.
The ophthalmologist conducted a thorough examination and asked many questions.
They recommended cataract removal and a trifocal lens replacement, which would allow me to see without glasses anymore.
The doctor mentioned that I might experience some glare initially, especially when driving at night, and that it would take some time to adjust.
I had the cataract removal and lens replacement on the 10th and started driving during the day on the 14th, and everything went perfectly. On the 18th, I drove at night for almost an hour.
